name: McWay Falls Overlook, Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park
highlight: An eighty-foot waterfall drops straight onto a crescent of sand in a cove the color of green glass. The overlook path runs a few hundred feet out from Highway 1 through a tunnel under the road, and there is no way down to the beach, so the view is the entire visit.

fact.verbatim: All film shoots at Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park and all other California State Parks are required to have a valid film permit issued by the California Film Commission (CFC). The term “film shoot” refers to both motion picture and still photography shoots.

permit.authority: California State Parks

blocker: Events, elopements, and filming will not be permitted/allowed at the Waterfall Overlook, the Waterfall Overlook Trail, McWay Falls, or Canyon Trail until further notice. (Updated December 15, 2024)
ineligibleReason: California State Parks: "Events, elopements, and filming will not be permitted/allowed at the Waterfall Overlook, the Waterfall Overlook Trail, McWay Falls, or Canyon Trail until further notice." (Updated December 15, 2024)

name: Soberanes Point, Garrapata State Park
highlight: Headland loops run out over black rock and open ocean about ten miles south of Carmel, with a short climb to a bench above the Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary. Sea lions and otters work the water below and gray whales pass close in winter.

fact.verbatim: Everything beyond what is listed above requires a permit from the California Film Commission and anyone engaged in commercial (profit and sale) photography on state property.

permit.authority: California State Parks

blocker: The Soberanes Trail is open exclusively from the main, gated trailhead on the east side of Highway 1, across from Gate 8 of the Garrapata Coastal Trail.

name: Razor Point Overlook, Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
highlight: Eroded sandstone fins and ravines drop away to the surf at the end of a half-mile trail through Torrey pines, the rarest pine in the country. The railed point sits directly above the beach with the lagoon behind you.

fact.verbatim: Everything beyond what is listed above requires a permit from the California Film Commission and anyone engaged in commercial (profit and sale) photography on state property.

permit.authority: California State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: Gates open at 07:15 a.m. and close at Sunset.

blocker: Torrey Pines SNR is currently unavailable as a Special Event location due the recent construction project.

name: Luscomb Point, Sunset Cliffs Natural Park
highlight: Sandstone cliffs run a mile and a half along the west edge of Point Loma, facing straight into the sunset with no land between you and the horizon. Dirt paths follow the rim past sea caves and blowholes; there are no restrooms and no railings.

fact.verbatim: Casual, amateur photographers, tourists, credentialed members of the media, or other members of the public who do not use vehicles or equipment or assert exclusive use of City property are not required to submit a Filming Registration Form.

permit.authority: City of San Diego Special Events and Filming Department

privacy.verbatim: The Luscomb Point area is named for Happy Luscomb, a local surfing personality. It is a favorite spot for sunset viewing and weddings, which can be permitted for up to 50 people. Parking is available on the street or at a number of small lots at the park site. There are no restrooms available.

name: Palace of Fine Arts Rotunda and Lagoon
highlight: A Beaux-Arts rotunda and colonnade stand in a curve around a lagoon in the Marina, with weeping figures turned inward on the tops of the columns. Swans and herons use the water and the reflection doubles the whole structure at first light.

fact.verbatim: All commercial film, video or photography (Film) production on Recreation and Park Department property requires a Film Permit. Commercial film production is defined as any activity that results in a film, video or photograph being sold or used for commercial purposes, or any activity involving filming or photography for which crew and/or talent is paid. This includes not-for-profit productions. This also includes wedding pictures if the wedding is not taking place on SFRPD property and the photographer is being paid. It does not include photography or video for personal use, however tripods, even for personal use, are restricted in certain areas.

permit.authority: San Francisco Recreation and Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: Park Hours: 5 a.m. to 11:45 p.m.

fee: $369 - Simple non-intrusive exterior still photography (per day, per site).

name: Shakespeare Garden, Golden Gate Park
highlight: A hedged garden off the Music Concourse, entered through an iron gate, with a brick path running to a sundial and benches set back under the foliage. The fencing and planting screen it from the rest of the park without closing it in.

fact.verbatim: All commercial film, video or photography (Film) production on Recreation and Park Department property requires a Film Permit. Commercial film production is defined as any activity that results in a film, video or photograph being sold or used for commercial purposes, or any activity involving filming or photography for which crew and/or talent is paid. This includes not-for-profit productions. This also includes wedding pictures if the wedding is not taking place on SFRPD property and the photographer is being paid. It does not include photography or video for personal use, however tripods, even for personal use, are restricted in certain areas.

permit.authority: San Francisco Recreation and Parks

privacy.verbatim: PUBLIC PARK: Wedding sites cannot be “closed to the public” due to each site being located in a public park.

fee: $369 - Simple non-intrusive exterior still photography (per day, per site).
blocker: Shakespeare Garden has a gate but must still remain unlocked at all times.

name: Griffith Observatory West Lawn and Terrace
highlight: Three copper domes sit on a terrace above the whole Los Angeles basin, with the Hollywood sign on the ridge to the west and the downtown towers straight ahead. The lawn below the building empties out well before the parking lot does.

fact.verbatim: Major commercial film and photography shoots can only take place on days the Observatory building is closed to the public (though the grounds are open). The Observatory has virtually no “back of house” areas where filming or photography can occur away from the public. Filming and photography in non-public areas of the building is prohibited.

permit.authority: City of Los Angeles Department of Recreation and Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: The Observatory’s main purpose is to serve the public, and we are open to the public 10-12 hours a day on all weekend days and most weekdays in pursuit of this mission.

privacy.verbatim: The tunnel and adjacent trails are NOT part of the Observatory grounds; they are under the jurisdiction of Griffith Park and the Park Film Office.

name: Shoreline Park Bluff, Santa Barbara
highlight: A long grass bluff above the harbor with a walking path along the edge, the Channel Islands stacked on the horizon and a stairway cut down to the sand. Gray whales pass close enough to watch from the lawn in winter and spring.

fact.verbatim: The City of Santa Barbara offers a one-stop permitting process with the Parks and Recreation Department acting as the lead in issuing photo and film permits for any location on City property.

permit.authority: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation

privacy.verbatim: One of our most popular parks overlooking the beach and harbor, Shoreline Park features a playground for two- to five-year-olds, large grassy areas, walking paths, views of the Channel Islands, whale watching area, a stairway to the beach, and reservable picnic areas.

name: Mendocino Headlands State Park Bluff Trail
highlight: A bluff trail wraps the town of Mendocino on three sides, past sea arches, tunnels and grass that runs right to the drop. The village water towers sit behind you and there is nothing but ocean in front.

fact.verbatim: Everything beyond what is listed above requires a permit from the California Film Commission and anyone engaged in commercial (profit and sale) photography on state property.

permit.authority: California State Parks

privacy.verbatim: For these reasons State Park units in the Sonoma-Mendocino Coast District do not allow launching, landing or the operation of drones on State Park property.

name: Point Cabrillo Light Station State Historic Park
highlight: A half-mile walk down a gravel road across open headland ends at a restored lighthouse and three original keepers' houses. The land runs out into the Pacific on three sides of the building.

fact.verbatim: Everything beyond what is listed above requires a permit from the California Film Commission and anyone engaged in commercial (profit and sale) photography on state property.

permit.authority: California State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: The preserve grounds are open for pedestrian use from sunrise to sunset daily.

privacy.verbatim: For these reasons State Park units in the Sonoma-Mendocino Coast District do not allow launching, landing or the operation of drones on State Park property.

name: Sonoma Overlook Trail, Montini Open Space Preserve
highlight: The trail climbs out of Mountain Cemetery a few blocks north of the Plaza through oak savanna to a bench on the hillside, with the vineyard floor of Sonoma Valley below and the Bay visible on a clear day. Benches sit at several points along the way.

fact.verbatim: A film permit is required for filming activity (the filming, video taping, photographing, or other similar process conducted for the making of motion pictures, television programs, commercial and nontheatrical productions) on location within the City. Certain exemptions apply.

permit.authority: City of Sonoma

crowdWindow.verbatim: The trail is open to the public for walking during daylight hours.

privacy.verbatim: Dogs, bikes, horses and smoking prohibited.

name: Mountain Station Observation Deck, Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
highlight: Rotating tram cars climb out of Chino Canyon from desert scrub into pine forest, and the deck at the top looks straight down onto the Coachella Valley floor and the street grid of Palm Springs. The temperature drops sharply on the way up.

fact.verbatim: Unauthorized photography, recording, or activities for commercial purposes.

permit.authority: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway

blocker: Other Items: Selfie sticks, tripods, flags, or banners are not allowed. Tripods or monopod stands exceeding a standard backpack size are prohibited.

name: Diamond Head (Lēʻahi) Summit, Diamond Head State Monument
highlight: The trail ends inside a 1911 fire control station on the crater rim, 560 feet above the crater floor. From the bunker the shoreline runs unbroken from Koko Head to Waiʻanae, with Waikīkī's towers small and pale below.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: With visitors to the park exceeding 3,000 people per day, Diamond Head is one of the most popular and heavily visited destinations in the state.

fee: $5 per person entry for non-Hawaii residents; $10 per vehicle non-resident parking (Hawaii residents free with ID). State film permit location fee: "parks and beaches under the Department of Land and Natural Resources / Division of State Parks have a $100/day nonrefundable fee" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/).
blocker: Liability insurance required with the film permit. Standard Film Permit applies here because the Film Office states "ALL STATE PARK LOCATIONS HAVE BEEN REMOVED FROM THE OAHU, MAUI AND KAUAI O&A SITE LIST" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/locations/openaccessible-sites/) — the faster Open & Accessible ePermit is not available at Diamond Head. Standard permits must be submitted at least five (5) business days ahead. If the proposal is staged as a ceremony/elopement rather than photography only, State Parks additionally requires a Special Use Permit submitted 45 days in advance.
accessNote: Entry and parking reservations are required for non-residents and sell out — a date can be impossible without one. Hawaii DLNR: "Entry and parking reservations required for non-residents (as of May 12th, 2022), plan accordingly." (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dsp/parks/oahu/diamond-head-state-monument/). Park hours 6:00 am to 6:00 pm daily; last entry 4:30 pm for the 4:00 pm reservation.

name: Nuʻuanu Pali Lookout, Nuʻuanu Pali State Wayside
highlight: The Koʻolau cliffs fall away 1,200 feet to the windward plain, with Kāneʻohe Bay laid out below. The trades funnel through the gap hard enough to lean against.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of State Parks

privacy.verbatim: Impressive view of windward Oʻahu from brink of pali (cliffs) at 1200 feet elevation in the Ko’olau Range. Winds are usually so strong that one can lean against the wall of wind.

fee: Non-resident parking $7.00 per vehicle; Hawaii residents no charge. State film permit location fee: "parks and beaches under the Department of Land and Natural Resources / Division of State Parks have a $100/day nonrefundable fee" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/).
blocker: Liability insurance required with the film permit. The Film Office removed "Nuuanu Pali State Wayside (Oahu)" from the DLNR Open and Accessible list (https://filmoffice.hawaii.gov/locations/openaccessible-sites/), so the fast O+A ePermit is not available here — a Standard Film Permit at five business days minimum is required.
accessNote: No reservation required. Gate hours are the constraint: "Daily 6:00am to 6:00pm" (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dsp/parks/oahu/nuuanu-pali-state-wayside/).

name: Mānoa Falls, Honolulu Watershed Forest Reserve
highlight: A short, consistently wet walk through bamboo and hau ends at a thin fall dropping into a shallow rock basin. The light arrives filtered green and the valley walls close in on both sides.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife

blocker: A second, slower permit may stack on top of the state film permit. DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife: "Commercial activities ranging from guided hikes and tours to photography may require additional permits. It is the individual’s sole responsibility to ensure that all applicable permits are held prior to commencement of regulated activities." DOFAW's general guideline is that "requests for permits should be submitted, at minimum, 90 days prior to the expected start of field work" (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dofaw/permits/). Confirm with the Oʻahu Branch whether a DOFAW permit is needed for your shoot.
accessNote: Jurisdiction note for planning: Mānoa Falls is a DOFAW trail, not a State Parks unit — DLNR lists it under the Honolulu Watershed Forest Reserve and states that "Diamond Head, ʻAiea Loop, Makapuʻu Lighthouse and Kaʻena Point Trails are all managed by DLNR Division of State Parks" while the Honolulu Watershed trails are DOFAW (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dofaw/oahu/faq/). No entry reservation is required for the trail itself.

name: Makapuʻu Point Lighthouse Lookout, Kaiwi State Scenic Shoreline
highlight: A paved mile of old lighthouse access road climbs to a headland 500 feet above the red-roofed Makapuʻu light. The lookout holds the whole southeastern coastline, and from November through May humpbacks work the channel below.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: Hawaii’s humpback whale season runs from November through May, with January through March being the peak whale-watching months.

fee: No entrance fee. State film permit location fee: "parks and beaches under the Department of Land and Natural Resources / Division of State Parks have a $100/day nonrefundable fee" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/).
blocker: Liability insurance required with the film permit. All Oʻahu state park locations were removed from the Open & Accessible list, so a Standard Film Permit (five business days minimum) is required rather than the fast O+A ePermit. The Makapuʻu tide pools below the trail are a closed area — DLNR: "The tide pools located at Kaiwi State Scenic Shoreline commonly referred to as the Makapu’u tide pools are in a CLOSED AREA and considered very dangerous."
accessNote: Gate hours limit the window: summer 7:00am to 7:45pm, winter 7:00am to 6:45pm; summer hours begin April 1, winter hours the day after Labor Day (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dsp/parks/oahu/kaiwi-state-scenic-shoreline/). No reservation system.

name: Lanikai Pillboxes, Kaʻiwa Ridge
highlight: Two WWII observation stations sit on a bare ridge above Kailua. From the upper roof the Mokulua islets sit offshore in shallow water and the windward coast runs from Waimānalo to Mokoliʻi.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR

crowdWindow.verbatim: But now with widespread advertising on travel websites and social media the trail is experiencing the same problems as many other O‘ahu hiking trails; it is being loved to death.

blocker: Jurisdiction is state but unusual, so confirm with the Film Office before booking a photographer. DLNR: "Though located on state land, this trail is not on the managed inventory of DLNR’s Na Ala Hele and Access Program" and "Today, the two pillboxes sit on DLNR land" (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/blog/2018/03/16/nr18-036/). Because it is not a Division of State Parks unit, the published $100/day State Parks location fee may not be the applicable one. Liability insurance is required with any state film permit.
accessNote: No reservation or entry fee, but the trail has been closed outright for structural repairs to the pillboxes before — DLNR closed it for at least 60 calendar days in 2018 (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/blog/2018/03/16/nr18-036/). Check DLNR trail notices before committing to a date.

name: Kualoa Regional Park
highlight: A flat run of lawn meets the water with the Koʻolau wall rising directly behind it. Mokoliʻi — the cone islet off the point — sits a few hundred yards offshore and takes the early light first.

fact.verbatim: Section 34. Permits. (a) Applicants desiring to use City parks properties for commercial filming purposes shall first secure a permit from the Department. (b) Permits shall be issued in the name of the commercial film company designated on the Certificate of Insurance. (c) Permits shall be non-transferable. (d) Daily, monthly, annual permits may be issued to still photographers shooting wedding ceremonies, portraits, scenics, etc., or if shooting does not involve any commercial product or the use of props such as birds, animals, etc.

permit.authority: City and County of Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation

blocker: Liability insurance. Honolulu DPR rule Section 37(a): "Each permit applicant must have in current force and effect an insurance policy, in which a combined limit of liability for bodily injury and property damage is $1 million per occurrence. The insurance certificate shall name the City and County of Honolulu and its officers and employees, and the State of Hawaii and its officers and employees as additional insured." A second permit may also be needed below the high-water mark — Section 37(c): "For beach parks owned or controlled by the City, the high-water mark shall be considered the makai boundary. Applicants shall be responsible to secure applicable commercial filming permits from the State Department of Land and Natural Resources and the State Department of Transportation for filming activities occurring makai of the high-water mark."
accessNote: No entry reservation, but the city application deadline is hard: "Application must be filed 3 weeks in advance to the DPR Permits Office" (https://www.honolulu.gov/parks/default/park-locations/182-site-dpr-cat/1758-park-use-permits.html). A proposal booked inside three weeks cannot be permitted on the city side.

name: Byodo-In Temple, Valley of the Temples
highlight: A full-scale replica of Japan's Byodo-In, its Phoenix Hall standing at the edge of a koi pond with the Koʻolau ridge rising almost vertically behind it. A three-ton brass bell hangs in its own house near the entrance and visitors ring it before going in.

fact.verbatim: Permits are required for all planned individual or group photo shoots, whether personal or professional, such as graduation, family portraits, special events, etc.

permit.authority: Byodo-In Temple Hawaii / Valley of the Temples Memorial Park (private property)

privacy.verbatim: Because the Byodo-In Temple is a place of prayer and meditation, as well as where memorial services are often conducted, we do request that visitors dress appropriately (no beach attire) and behave as you would in a place of worship (no running, yelling, throwing rocks, climbing trees, bothering wildlife, etc.).

fee: General Admission $10.00 (age 13-64); Seniors $8.00 (age 65 & up); Children $6.00 (age 2-12); parking $6 per hour. Kamaʻāina rates with valid Hawaii ID. Photo-shoot permit fee is not published — obtain the permit reservation form from the gift shop.
blocker: A permit is required even for a personal, unpaid photo shoot here — the rule covers "whether personal or professional." Note this is private land, so no state film permit applies: "Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property" (https://filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/). The temple's own permit governs instead.
accessNote: Admission is ticketed and hours are short: "The Byodo-In Temple is open daily from 8:30am – 4:30pm with the last entrance at 4:15pm" (https://byodo-in.com/visit/). Sunset proposals are not possible here.

name: Paʻiloa Black Sand Beach, Waiʻānapanapa State Park
highlight: Black sand set between low lava headlands, with a natural stone arch, blowholes and a hala forest along the coastal trail behind it. The water reads very bright against the rock.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: Visitors making parking reservations will be required to select a time slot, to spread out visitation across the day.

fee: Non-residents $5.00 per person entry plus $10 per vehicle parking; Hawaii residents free with driver's licence or ID. State film permit location fee: "parks and beaches under the Department of Land and Natural Resources / Division of State Parks have a $100/day nonrefundable fee" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/).
blocker: Liability insurance required with the film permit. "Waianapanapa State Park (Maui)" was removed from the DLNR Open and Accessible list (https://filmoffice.hawaii.gov/locations/openaccessible-sites/), so a Standard Film Permit — five business days minimum — is required rather than the fast O+A ePermit.
accessNote: This is the hardest availability constraint in the set. DLNR: "All visitors and commercial operators will need to make reservations to enter the popular Waiʻānapana State Park on Maui, beginning on March 1." The park page is headed "RESERVATIONS REQUIRED" and reservations are time-slotted (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dsp/parks/maui/waianapanapa-state-park/). Reserve at https://gostateparks.hawaii.gov/waianapanapa before fixing a date. Hours 7:00am–6:00pm daily.

name: ʻĪao Needle Lookout, ʻĪao Valley State Monument
highlight: A paved 0.6-mile walk ends at a rail facing Kukaʻemoku, the green spire that rises 1,200 feet straight off the valley floor. Cloud moves through the gap above it most afternoons.

fact.verbatim: Film permits and insurance are required for all filming activity, commercial, educational or non-profit projects which take place within the State’s jurisdiction.  Film permits are not required for photography or video that is only for personal use or which takes place on private property.

permit.authority: Hawaii Film Office (Department of Business, Economic Development & Tourism), permitting on behalf of Hawaii DLNR Division of State Parks

privacy.verbatim: This valley is rich in cultural and spiritual values and is the site of the battle of Kepaniwai where the forces of Kamehameha I conquered the Maui army in 1790.

fee: Non-residents $5 per person entry plus $10 per vehicle parking; Hawaii residents free with Hawaii DL or ID. State film permit location fee: "parks and beaches under the Department of Land and Natural Resources / Division of State Parks have a $100/day nonrefundable fee" (filmoffice.hawaii.gov/permit-procedures/).
blocker: Liability insurance required with the film permit. ʻĪao also sits inside a designated historic district, and the Maui Film Office states: "Historic Districts: Any filming activity in certain parts of Lahaina, Iao Valley, Wailuku or any other designated historic district must be cleared through the Maui Film Office" (https://www.mauicounty.gov/DocumentCenter/View/12482/Maui-County-Film-Permit-Application-Handbook). Expect a second clearance on top of the state permit.
accessNote: Reservations gate the date for visitors from out of state. DLNR: "*Advance reservations are required for out-of-State residents. Reservations can be made at https://gostateparks.hawaii.gov." (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/dsp/parks/maui/iao-valley-state-monument/). Hours 7:00 am to 6:00 pm daily.

name: Hoʻokipa Lookout, Hoʻokipa Beach Park
highlight: A low bluff above Hoʻokipa's reef break on Maui's north shore, with sailors working the outside break and the coast running west toward Pāʻia. Late afternoon puts the sun straight down the length of the shoreline.

fact.verbatim: County Parks Permits: Cover any production activities taking place in a county park or recreation area. A fee of $100 to $300 per day applies, depending on the activity taking place.

permit.authority: County of Maui, Office of Economic Development — Maui Film Office (county park); Hawaii DLNR / Hawaii Film Office for the sandy beach below
permit.authorityContact: Maui Film Office, (808) 270-8237, filmmaui@mauicounty.gov — https://www.mauicounty.gov/DocumentCenter/View/12482/Maui-County-Film-Permit-Application-Handbook ; Maui County DPR Permits Main Office (808) 270-7389

fee: $100 to $300 per day for a county parks permit, depending on the activity (Maui Film Office handbook). No entry or parking fee is published for the park itself.
blocker: Split jurisdiction — the grassy bluff and the sand are governed by different agencies, and the Maui handbook is written for film production, not proposals, so it does not say whether a two-person engagement shoot needs a permit at all. Maui Film Office: "Although there are exceptions, most beach parks (the grassy areas fronting sandy beaches) are on county property" and "State Permits: Cover all sandy beaches, airports, harbors and certain beach parks and any filming of marine activities." Hawaii DLNR Land Division adds the general rule for the sand: "The general rule (with very few exceptions) is that where you have a county park, the shoreline is still under the jurisdiction of the State. Therefore, if you want your event on the sandy beach, you will need a permit from Wiki Permits. The county cannot issue you a permit for the sandy beach because that land is not under their jurisdiction." (https://dlnr.hawaii.gov/ld/commercial-activities/). Call the Maui Film Office to confirm before hiring a photographer.

name: Promontory Point
highlight: A stone-rimmed peninsula that pushes out into Lake Michigan at 55th Street, so the downtown skyline sits across open water to the north rather than looming overhead. Alfred Caldwell's limestone council rings and meadow are behind you; the water is at your feet.

fact.verbatim: A permit is required for the following types of filming and photography: Non-commercial use, such as engagement, wedding, and other special occasions

permit.authority: Chicago Park District

crowdWindow.verbatim: Note: Media Permit availability may be limited during peak periods. Additional fees may apply for indoor locations which vary by site.

fee: Non-Commercial Filming/Photography: $45 (per location, per hour), No Fee security deposit, insurance not required. The same page states "Filming & Photography Permit Pricing includes a $35 Application Fee + Permit Fees" but the application-payment step on that page is labeled "a non-refundable $45 Permit Application Fee" — confirm the current application fee with the Park District before budgeting.
accessNote: Promontory Point is NOT one of the twelve locations the Park District lets you self-reserve online for a non-commercial photography permit, so it goes through the general queue: "For All Other Filming & Photography Complete Step 1 & Step 2: Click on the following button to pay a non-refundable $45 Permit Application Fee now, and secure your spot in the queue." (https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/filming-photography-permits). Park hours are posted on the park page as 6:00 am-11:00 pm daily.

name: Lincoln Park Conservatory
highlight: An 1890s glass house with four rooms — Palm House, Fern Room, Orchid House, Show House — where the air is warm and wet and the light comes down green through forty-foot palms. It reads the same in February as in June, which is the point.

fact.verbatim: A permit is required for the following types of filming and photography: Non-commercial use, such as engagement, wedding, and other special occasions

permit.authority: Chicago Park District

crowdWindow.verbatim: Note: Media Permit availability may be limited during peak periods. Additional fees may apply for indoor locations which vary by site.

fee: Non-Commercial Filming/Photography: $45 (per location, per hour). Conservatory admission itself is free ("Admission is free." — https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/parks-facilities/lincoln-park-conservatory), but see accessNote — entry is timed and must be reserved separately.
accessNote: TWO separate bookings are required and a full house can turn you away at the door: "Reservations are required to enter the conservatories. Prior to booking a non-commercial media permit, make a reservation online for entry for all participants to ensure there is space available on the day and time of your permit. Failure to include the entire party may result in you being turned away due to lack of space. Reservations are available 30 days out. Both the proof of reservation and permit will be required to show when arriving at a conservatory for photography." (https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/filming-photography-permits). The park page also currently notes: "The Conservatory is open with timed entry and adjusted hours."

name: Museum Campus Skyline View (Solidarity Drive, by the Adler Planetarium)
highlight: The causeway out to the Adler puts the entire Loop in one frame across the harbor — Willis, the Aon, the Blue Cross tower — with sailboats in the foreground and nothing built behind you. It is the postcard angle, and it is a public sidewalk.

fact.verbatim: A permit is required for the following types of filming and photography: Non-commercial use, such as engagement, wedding, and other special occasions

permit.authority: Chicago Park District

crowdWindow.verbatim: Note: Media Permit availability may be limited during peak periods. Additional fees may apply for indoor locations which vary by site.

fee: Non-Commercial Filming/Photography: $45 (per location, per hour)
accessNote: This is one of the twelve locations the Park District lets you self-reserve online: "Reserve a permit for non-commercial photography (such as engagement, wedding, and other special occasions) at the following locations by clicking on the Reserve button below. ... Museum Campus Skyline View (Solidarity Dr.)" (https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/filming-photography-permits). Note the Adler Planetarium building and grounds are a private institution, not Park District land — the permit covers the Solidarity Drive skyline-view location.

name: Chicago Riverwalk
highlight: A continuous promenade a full story below street level, running from Lake Shore Drive to Lake Street with the bridgehouses and the river-facing walls of the Loop rising straight up on both sides. The city noise is above you; the water is beside you.

fact.verbatim: Can I take photos for a special event on the Riverwalk? The Riverwalk is free and open to the public. Please be respectful, courteous and mindful of everyone who is also enjoying the Riverwalk. Vendor areas may have a separate policy please inquire with a vendor or contact us.

permit.authority: City of Chicago — Chicago Riverwalk (Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events / Chicago Film Office)

crowdWindow.verbatim: What are the Riverwalk hours? The Riverwalk is open from 6 am to 11 pm.

accessNote: DIFFERENT AUTHORITY from the three Chicago Park District rows above — the Riverwalk is City of Chicago, not Park District, and its rules do not carry over in either direction. A personal proposal needs no permit per the FAQ; a crewed shoot goes through the Chicago Film Office (https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dca/supp_info/permits.html). Riverwalk vendor patios are separately controlled: "Vendor areas may have a separate policy please inquire with a vendor or contact us."

name: Arch Rock
highlight: A limestone arch standing about 150 feet above the east shore, with Lake Huron showing turquoise through the opening. The overlook platform is reached on foot, by bike, or by horse — there is no other way to arrive.

fact.verbatim: Arrangements for filming, taping, recording, interviewing or photographing at MSHP must be made several days in advance through the Chief of Marketing.

permit.authority: Mackinac State Historic Parks (Mackinac Island State Park Commission)

accessNote: Arch Rock is explicitly named as Mackinac Island State Park Commission land in the film-and-photography guidelines: "These guidelines are designed for those requesting to film on MSHP sites as well as all land and buildings owned by the Mackinac Island State Park Commission including but not limited to: ... Mackinac Island State Park (including, but not limited to) – Arch Rock". YOUR DATE MAY BE HARDER THAN IT LOOKS: the island has no car access — "Motor vehicles were banned on Mackinac Island in 1898." — so everything hinges on the ferry schedule, and MSHP's staffed season is limited: "MSHP's sites are open from early-May through mid-October. Scouting and/or filming on site before or after this time is discouraged due to limited staff and non-winterized buildings. Off-season requests will be reviewed individually and must be made at least a week in advance." (all https://www.mackinacparks.com/about/media/film-and-photography-guidelines-2/)

name: Lake Michigan Overlook, Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore (FEDERAL LAND)
highlight: A sand bluff 450 feet straight above the water, with the lake filling the whole western horizon and no shoreline development in sight. On a clear day the bluffs at Empire and the sweep of Platte Bay are visible to the south.

fact.verbatim: All filming, still photography, and audio recording is treated the same under the new law. It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

permit.authority: National Park Service — Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore (FEDERAL)

blocker: FEDERAL LAND — this is National Park Service jurisdiction, not Michigan DNR and not a county park. Note the park's own Special Use Permits page still reads "The National Park Service (NPS) requires a permit for activities not normally associated with a visit to Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore. This includes activities such as, commercial photography, memorials, first amendment activities, and powerless flight." (https://www.nps.gov/slbe/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm) — that park page has not caught up with the NPS-wide rule quoted above. Call the park if a hired photographer is involved.
accessNote: The overlook is reached from Stop #9 on the one-way Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive: "A paved path through a section of maple-beech forest leads to the approach to Lake Michigan Overlook. This paved trail becomes loose sand before reaching the top of the dune." (https://www.nps.gov/places/000/lake-michigan-overlook-pssd9.htm). A park entrance pass is required for the Lakeshore.
seasonalClosure: The driving approach closes for roughly half the year: "The Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive is open to vehicles seasonally. Generally: late May until late October. During the winter and spring, the drive is open for hiking and walk-in recreation during the vehicle closure." (https://www.nps.gov/places/000/pierce-stocking-scenic-drive.htm) — off-season you can still reach the overlook, but on foot over a 7.4-mile loop road.

name: Cave Point County Park
highlight: Wave-cut dolomite ledges dropping straight into Lake Michigan, with sea caves undercut below the rim you are standing on. It faces east, so it is a sunrise spot, and in winter the spray freezes onto the rock in sheets.

fact.verbatim: Various parks may be reserved, (but not closed to the public), for weddings, reunions, birthdays, private and company picnics and other events.

permit.authority: Door County Facilities and Parks Department

crowdWindow.verbatim: Well-known for its wave-worn Dolomite/limestone ledges, underwater caves and stirring view of Lake Michigan, the park is a popular attraction for residents and visitors alike. The site is a popular location for weddings as well. Fishermen, skilled scuba divers, photography buffs, and nature observers find the park a great delight.

privacy.verbatim: Various parks may be reserved, (but not closed to the public), for weddings, reunions, birthdays, private and company picnics and other events.

accessNote: Reserving space here never buys you privacy — the county states plainly that reserved parks are "not closed to the public." Reservations are also unforgiving: "All reservations are taken on a first-come, first served basis and are Nonrefundable." (https://www.co.door.wi.gov/766/Door-County-Park-Rentals). Cave Point is a small park — "Cave Point County Park consists of 18.6 acres, including 900 feet of shoreline" — and the ledges are genuinely dangerous: "Use caution, as rocks are slippery when wet or covered with ice." Door County's parks ordinance (Chapter 12) contains no photography-permit provision at all, which is why this row is amber rather than green — call Facilities and Parks before assuming a hired photographer is fine.

name: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park — Lake Superior shoreline overlooks
highlight: The 1910 lighthouse sits on a 130-foot cliff above Lake Superior, and the park's shoreline lookouts frame it from below and to the side. Pebble Beach at the base is a cove of flat, water-smoothed stones.

fact.verbatim: Film and photography permits ARE NOT required for the following activities, unless the filming/photography meets any criteria on the list above: Coverage of news, by news media. Visitors taking photos or videos for their own personal use.

permit.authority: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Trails

fee: A Minnesota state park vehicle permit is required: "All vehicles entering a state park must display a valid year-round or one-day Minnesota state park vehicle permit affixed to the lower right hand corner of the windshield." (https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state_parks/rules.html)
blocker: The permit exemption above is conditional. The DNR's list of activities that DO require a permit includes filming or photography that "Involves the use of a prop, compensated model(s) or actor(s), or any set" and that "Potentially disrupts normal visitor activities or inconveniences other visitors" (https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state_parks/rules.html) — a staged setup with props may cross that line even though a personal proposal does not. "The application review process may take up to 30 days."
accessNote: TWO AUTHORITIES ON ONE SITE — the state park is Minnesota DNR, but the lighthouse compound itself is not: "The lighthouse site is maintained by the Minnesota Historical Society (MNHS) and includes the Fog Signal Building, three keeper's houses and the Visitor Center. Tours of the sites are available daily through the summer season for a fee." (https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state_parks/split_rock_lighthouse/things_to_do.html). The DNR photography rule above governs the park's shoreline and trails; anything inside the MNHS-run lighthouse site needs to be cleared with MNHS separately. Park hours: "Park hours 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., 365 days a year."

name: Minnehaha Falls
highlight: A single fifty-odd-foot drop into a limestone gorge inside the city, with a stone-and-iron overlook at the lip and a stair down to the streambed below. The pergola garden above it is the formal counterpoint.

fact.verbatim: Still Photography: It applies to low impact (minimal props and equipment) photo session for personal use by a private individual, these are typically to document a time in your life – not for high-traffic viewing or advertising.

permit.authority: Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board

fee: Individual/Group Portrait Fees: $47 per 1.5 hours; $315 annual. Commercial Fees: $315 per day and location. Change Order Fee: "You will need a new permit. $35 per change order" (https://www.minneapolisparks.org/permits/photography__filming_permits/)
accessNote: MPRB nowhere mentions proposals or engagements — the closest category is the "Individual/Group Portrait" still-photo permit, which is why this row is amber. Lead time: "Step 3: Your application will be reviewed by MPRB staff in the order in which it was received. Please plan on submitting your application at least 10 days prior to your requested date(s)." And the permit is location-locked: "You are limited to the physical park location your permit lists, unless otherwise stated in the notes a permit. For example, you may not take photos at Lake Nokomis if your permit lists only Minnehaha Park as your permitted location." No insurance for personal work: "Still Photography: No, for personal use photography we do not require insurance" (all https://www.minneapolisparks.org/permits/photography__filming_permits/)

name: Enchanted Rock Summit
highlight: A bare pink granite dome 425 feet above the Hill Country floor, climbed on open rock with no trees and no railing. From the top the horizon is unbroken in every direction, and at dusk the granite holds its heat and its color.

fact.verbatim: Media production is any audio, video, photo­graphic or digital recording including still photography, digital imaging, filming or video recording. Examples include docu­men­taries, independent or student films, scenic photography, motion picture pro­duc­tions, commercials, marketing videos or photos, drone video or photos, or any other commercial filming activity.

permit.authority: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department — Enchanted Rock State Natural Area

crowdWindow.verbatim: Parks are most likely to fill on weekends and school holidays. Capacity limits are in place to protect you, the park's natural and cultural resources, and its infrastructure.

blocker: The route to the top is weather-dependent: "The Summit Trail may close in wet weather." (https://tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/enchanted-rock)
accessNote: YOUR DATE CAN BE IMPOSSIBLE. TPWD names this park specifically: "No. You can purchase a daily entrance pass at the park if any are available. However, many parks have capacity limits and will close to drop-in day-use visitors once they reach that limit. Very popular parks such as Enchanted Rock may sell out days in advance." The fix is to buy ahead: "Guarantee entry to a state park with a day pass. We highly recommend buying a day pass in advance for popular parks. Day passes are available up to 30 days before your visit." But note the limit of that guarantee: "No. Your day pass only guarantees entrance into the park. It does not guarantee access to specific day-use areas or parking lots." (all https://tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/park-reservation-information/day-pass-faqs). Separately, TPWD's media-production application window is long: "Submit completed applications up to one year and not less than 90 days before your event." (https://tpwd.texas.gov/state-parks/park-information/park-requests-application) — TPWD publishes no personal-proposal exemption, so if a paid photographer is coming, call before you count on it.

name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
highlight: A collapsed grotto where Hamilton Creek drops fifty feet off an overhanging limestone dome into a jade-green pool. Ferns and travertine hang from the underside of the arch; the whole thing is invisible until you are almost in it.

fact.verbatim: Reservations are not valid for commercial use or for shuttle.

permit.authority: Travis County Parks (Travis County Transportation and Natural Resources)

crowdWindow.verbatim: Reservations Required to Enter Preserve Every Day March - October Every day November - February Weekends and Travis County Holidays Morning Reservation Period 9:00 am - 12:30 pm Afternoon Reservation Period 2:00 pm - 5:30 pm

fee: Reservation Fee per Vehicle: $12 (1 vehicle max, 8 people max). Per Person Entrance Fees: $8 per adult (13 to 61 years of age), $3 per senior (62 years of age and older), $0 per child (12 years of age and younger). "Cash only at the preserve. Credit and debit cards are not accepted. All fees are non-refundable." (https://parks.traviscountytx.gov/parks/hamilton-pool-preserve)
blocker: Part of the site is currently closed outright: "The section of trail that goes underneath the overhanging cliff at the pool is closed for safety concerns. Visitors can access the beach, but cannot walk all the way around the pool to below the waterfall. Rocks have been falling from the cliffs above the trail. We continue to consult with geologists about this hazard." (https://parks.traviscountytx.gov/parks/hamilton-pool-preserve)
accessNote: THE HARDEST DATE IN THIS SET. You cannot walk up: "Reservations are required every day of the week to visit Hamilton Pool Preserve. Please make your reservation online before arriving at the preserve." The booking window is finite: "You can now make Hamilton Pool Preserve reservations online for dates through September 2026. Reservations for dates in October 2026 and beyond are not available yet." And the water itself is never promised: "As always, whether swimming at the pool will be allowed depends on factors beyond our control, such as bacteria levels and recent rain. Water access is never guaranteed with a reservation. Even when swimming is not allowed, the preserve is open for hiking and reservations are still required." Timing is rigid: "Visitors cannot remain in the preserve after their reservation period ends. Please arrive at least an hour before your reservation period ends to give yourself time to enjoy the preserve. No entry allowed after the reservation time period is past." And a hired photographer is a real question mark: "Reservations are not valid for commercial use or for shuttle." (all https://parks.traviscountytx.gov/parks/hamilton-pool-preserve)

name: Mount Bonnell at Covert Park
highlight: About a hundred stone steps up to a limestone bluff 780-odd feet over Lake Austin, with the river bending below and the hills folding away west. It faces the sunset squarely, which is why everyone else is also there at 7pm.

fact.verbatim: Photo session permits are required for ANY posed/portrait or similar photo shoots at the following parks which experience high volumes of public use: Auditorium Shores Mayfield Park Mt. Bonnell at Cover Park Zilker Metropolitan Park Zilker Botanical Garden

permit.authority: City of Austin Parks and Recreation Department

fee: $50 per 2 hour session
blocker: "Sessions NOT permitted during special events or holidays." (https://www.austintexas.gov/parks/special-events-policies-and-procedures)
accessNote: Booking window is narrow at both ends: "$50 per 2 hour session - book online 4 days or up to 30 days prior. Sessions NOT permitted during special events or holidays." Austin also lists Mt. Bonnell among the parks "which experience high volumes of public use" — the permit is a queue for a busy overlook, not a private booking. If a paid photographer is involved, note Austin's separate commercial-activity rule and its teeth: "COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY means to advertise or provide a good, service, class, or instructional activity for compensation. ... Fines: $100-$500 fine, $250 minimum fine during a special event, Class C Misdemeanor." (all https://www.austintexas.gov/parks/special-events-policies-and-procedures). Note the city's own page spells the park "Cover Park" — the site is Covert Park.

name: Garden of the Gods Observation Trail, Shawnee National Forest (FEDERAL LAND)
highlight: A quarter-mile of flagstone across the top of a sandstone bluff, past Camel Rock and Devil's Smokestack, with the Shawnee Hills running to the horizon. The rock is banded and wind-cut, and the drop-offs are unfenced.

fact.verbatim: A De Minimis Use authorization may be issued for filming activities involving six to eight individuals, provided all conditions in Section 1(a)(5)(A)-(H) are met. No fee or cost recovery applies in these cases.

permit.authority: USDA Forest Service — Shawnee National Forest, Hidden Springs Ranger District

blocker: FEDERAL LAND, AND NOT THE SAME RULE AS A NATIONAL PARK. This is US Forest Service, not National Park Service. The Forest Service does not publish the NPS "eight or fewer individuals / permits and fees are not required" language, and its own guidance is a discretionary authorization — "may be issued" — so a proposal shoot here is genuinely unresolved on paper. The agency's instruction is to ask: "Contact your local Forest Service office for information on how to apply for a De Minimis Use Authorization or a Special Use Permit." (https://www.fs.usda.gov/working-with-us/contracts-commercial-permits/filming)
accessNote: Roughly a 2h15m drive southeast of St. Louis — the nearest catalog anchor, but it is a day trip, not a city outing. Hours: "Picnic area and Observation Trail hours of operation - 6 a.m. to 10 p.m." and "No overnight parking is allowed in picnic area or Observation Trail parking lots." No entry permit is needed for the adjacent wilderness — "No permit required for entering or camping in Garden of the Gods Wilderness." — but that is an access rule, not a photography rule. Also note: "Disposable food and beverage containers are not permitted on the Observation Trail." (so no champagne bottle on the rocks) and "Caution should be used due to the high cliffs in the area." (all https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/shawnee/recreation/garden-gods-recreation-area)

name: Garden of the Gods — Sentinel Plaza & Three Graces
highlight: Red sandstone fins stand straight up out of the grass with Pikes Peak framed behind them. The Central Garden paths are paved and nearly flat, and the city designates six small plazas here — Sentinel, Three Graces, High Point among them — for brief ceremonies.

fact.verbatim: There is no charge for the 6 areas listed below.  All are on a first come, first served basis. No reservations/permits available.

permit.authority: City of Colorado Springs Parks, Recreation and Cultural Services

privacy.verbatim: Tourists and other groups may be at the same site.  Please be respectful of other park users.

fee: No charge for the six designated areas; first come, first served
blocker: Do not bring in any tables, tents, arches, trellises, etc.
accessNote: The city caps informal gatherings before a permit kicks in: "If you plan to have more than 50 people, you will need to rent a pavilion or apply for a Special Event Permit." (https://coloradosprings.gov/parks/page/weddings-parks). The six Garden of the Gods areas carry their own posted capacities, from 20 people at Three Graces Plaza and High Point to 40 at Jaycee Plaza.

name: Hanging Lake
highlight: A turquoise lake held on a travertine shelf above Glenwood Canyon, with Spouting Rock pouring out of the cliff just behind it. Getting there is the hard part: "It climbs 1200 feet in 1.2 miles, follows multiple switchbacks, and crosses seven bridges."

fact.verbatim: A time-specific reservation is required for each visitor

permit.authority: USDA Forest Service — White River National Forest

fee: Reservations are $12/person April 30 - October 31; $10/person November 1 - March 31
blocker: Hikers must have their own vehicle parked at the trailhead. Uber, taxis, and drop-offs are not permitted due to potential emergency evacuations. There is no shuttle service to the Hanging Lake parking area.
accessNote: There is no sunrise or sunset slot, and no walk-up. "Reservations are available hourly from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with a 3-hour hiking window." and "You must arrive within 30 minutes before or after your reservation time or you will not be allowed entry." (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/hanging-lake). Forest Order WRNF 2019-06 also makes it an offense to be on the trail "without possessing a permit specifically exempting the act" (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/alerts/hanging-lake-occupancy-and-use).

name: Bridal Veil Falls & the Telluride box canyon
highlight: The falls drop straight off the headwall that closes Telluride's box canyon, with a stone powerhouse perched on the lip above them. The trail starts at the Valley View parking area east of town and climbs steeply on old mine road.

fact.verbatim: Maximum size for non-commercial groups is 20 and commercial / industrial use is not permitted.

permit.authority: San Miguel County / Town of Telluride (Bridal Veil Trail)

blocker: commercial / industrial use is not permitted
accessNote: Half the year is off the table on the trail: "Seasonal closure: December 1 - April 30." The land manager is a partnership, not one agency — "This trail is the result of a cooperative effort with the Town of Telluride, Idarado Mining Company, Telluride Mountain Club and San Miguel County." Because commercial use is barred outright, a paid photographer is a question to put to the county before booking one (https://www.sanmiguelcountyco.gov/293/Trails).

name: Dream Lake, Rocky Mountain National Park
highlight: A shallow lake pinched between Hallett Peak and Flattop Mountain, reached in "1.1 mi (1.8 km)" with "474 ft (144 m)" of gain from the Bear Lake trailhead. The wind off the water is close to constant; morning is when it lies flat enough to mirror the peaks.

fact.verbatim: All filming, still photography, and audio recording is treated the same under the new law. It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

permit.authority: National Park Service — Rocky Mountain National Park

crowdWindow.verbatim: Bear Lake Parking fills early in the day year-round. The parking area is often full by 9 a.m each day.

accessNote: No photo permit is needed, but you cannot drive to the trailhead without a separate reservation in season: "Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road Reservations are needed to enter the Bear Lake Road Corridor between the hours of 5 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily beginning on Friday, May 22 through Sunday, October 18, 2026." They are not first-choice-of-date guaranteed — "Timed entry reservations are released on a first-come, first-served basis on Recreation.gov", with a last-chance batch at "7 p.m. MDT on the night before a desired arrival date" (https://www.nps.gov/romo/planyourvisit/timed-entry-permit-system.htm).

name: Hidden Lake Overlook, Logan Pass
highlight: The trail leaves from behind the Logan Pass Visitor Center on "wooden boardwalk and packed soil" — "1.3 miles (2.1 km), one way" and "608 ft (185 m)" up — to a railing above Hidden Lake with Bearhat Mountain on the far side. Mountain goats are common on the boardwalk.

fact.verbatim: All filming, still photography, and audio recording is treated the same under the new law. It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

permit.authority: National Park Service — Glacier National Park

accessNote: No vehicle reservation this year — "Vehicle reservations are not required in 2026." (https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/goingtothesunroad.htm) — but you are on a clock at the top. "The three-hour parking limit will be implemented July 1, 2026 through Labor Day, September 7, 2026 and will be enforced 24 hours each day", and "After parking, visitors must then obtain a free, timestamped parking permit from the parking permit kiosk" (https://www.nps.gov/glac/planyourvisit/visiting-loganpass-2026.htm).
seasonalClosure: Logan Pass is only reachable by road for part of the year, and the opening date is set by plowing, not by calendar. NPS records list openings as early as May 16 (1987) and as late as July 13 (2020 and 2022), with footnote (f): "Pre-established closing date set for Logan Pass. Pass closes to vehicle use on third Monday in October, weather permitting." (https://www.nps.gov/glac/learn/news/logan-pass-opening-and-closing-dates.htm)

name: Kasha-Katuwe Tent Rocks National Monument
highlight: Cone-shaped pumice hoodoos, some still wearing the boulder that made them — "the tent rock formations vary in height from a few feet up to 90 feet." The Canyon Trail threads a slot before a "steep (630-ft) climb to the mesa top for excellent views of the Sangre de Cristo, Jemez, Sandia mountains and the Rio Grande Valley."

fact.verbatim: Entry into the monument is by reservation only, Thursdays through Mondays between 8:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m.

permit.authority: Bureau of Land Management, Rio Puerco Field Office (with Pueblo de Cochiti)

fee: BLM ticket reservation $6.00 per person (includes a $1.00 administrative fee), plus a separate Cochiti Pueblo Tribal Access Pass at "$20/person over age 16; $10/person 2-16 years old; and free for visitors under 2 years old"
blocker: Access to the Monument may be closed by order of the Cochiti Tribal Governor. Closures will be posted at the gate.
accessNote: A sunrise or sunset proposal here is impossible. It is "Day Use Only": "Check in begins no earlier than 7:45 a.m. with pilot vehicles leading visitors into the Monument starting at 8:00 a.m.  The last pilot car will leave the Cochiti Visitor Center at 1:00 p.m. All visitors must exit the Monument by 4:00 p.m." Two separate permits are needed, not one — "The Cochiti Pueblo Tribal Access Pass and the BLM Ticket Reservation are separate, and visitors must have both permits to access the Monument." Tickets are capped: "Visitors are encouraged to plan ahead and make reservations early as tickets are limited." (https://www.blm.gov/visit/kktr)
seasonalClosure: Closed "Dec. 15 – Jan. 31 (seasonal closure)", closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays year-round, plus Easter weekend, May 3, July 13 and 14, July 25, Nov. 1, Thanksgiving Day — and "The Monument may also be closed for no more than three additional cultural days identified by the Pueblo." (https://www.blm.gov/visit/kktr)

name: Rio Grande Gorge Bridge
highlight: US 64 crosses on a steel arch over a gorge the BLM describes as 800 feet deep, with walkways on both sides of the deck. Behind you the Taos Plateau runs dead flat in sage to the Sangre de Cristos.

permit.authority: Bureau of Land Management, Taos Field Office (Río Grande del Norte National Monument)

accessNote: The BLM publishes no permit rule for photography or gatherings at this site — its own page says only "Open year-round" and, on fees, "Contact the field office for more information." The bridge deck itself is state highway right-of-way rather than BLM-managed land, so the answer can differ on the span versus the rim. Call the Taos Field Office at 575-758-8851 before planning anything with a photographer or a group (https://www.blm.gov/visit/rgdnnm).

name: Bell Rock from Courthouse Vista
highlight: Bell Rock is the rounded buttress right off SR 179, and the Bell Rock Pathway out of Courthouse Vista is wide and near-level — you can be standing on open red slickrock with Courthouse Butte behind you within ten minutes of the car.

fact.verbatim: Permits are not required for a wedding when: 1. Fewer than 75 people are in attendance with no paid service providers (planners, ministers, musicians, equipment vendors, etc.), and no sound equipment.

permit.authority: USDA Forest Service — Coconino National Forest, Red Rock Ranger District

fee: $5 per vehicle per day / $15 per week / $20 per annual (Red Rock Pass, Courthouse Vista trailhead)
accessNote: You cannot park at the trailhead without a pass: "Red Rock Pass or America the Beautiful Pass is required to park at the trailhead." (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/coconino/recreation/courthouse-vista). On the permit question, the Forest Service does not publish a proposal rule — its own wording is that "A special use permit is required for commercial filming or photography on National Forest System lands under certain circumstances" and that a permit is not needed "if five or fewer people are involved in the film and photography project and are physically on site." Whether a hired proposal photographer counts is a call for the Red Rock Ranger District, not for us (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/coconino/permits).

name: Havasu Falls, Havasupai Indian Reservation
highlight: Blue-green water pouring over travertine into pools the color of glass, on the Havasupai Tribe's land inside the Grand Canyon's side country. There is no road: "It is an 8-mile hike with very significant elevation change between the trailhead and Supai Village", dropping from 5,200 feet at Hualapai Hilltop to 3,205 feet in the village, with the campground and falls further still.

fact.verbatim: PERMITS ARE REQUIRED FOR ALL VISITORS

permit.authority: Havasupai Tribe

fee: Campground permits are $455 per person for 3 nights. Lodge permits are $2,277 per lodge room for 3 nights – up to four people.
blocker: Photography, filming, documenting, or recording using any means for commercial purposes is also prohibited.
accessNote: This is not a park and not a national monument — it is a sovereign nation with its own permit regime, and it is the one place on this list where a specific date is often simply unavailable. highlight: A short paved ramp off Highway 190 opens onto a field of eroded golden badlands, ridge after wrinkled ridge, with the dark spire of Manly Beacon standing out of the middle of it. The rock lights up first at sunrise, when the crowd is a handful of people and the Panamints are still in shadow.

In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

accessNote: The overlook itself is open year-round, but Death Valley notes that filming activity along State Highway 190 can pull in Caltrans permitting and California Highway Patrol traffic control — stay on the overlook and off the roadway. Drones are separately prohibited: "Launching, landing, or operating an unmanned aircraft" is not allowed (https://www.nps.gov/deva/learn/management/filming-and-photography.htm).

name: Canyon Junction Bridge, Zion National Park
highlight: From the bridge where the Pa'rus Trail meets the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive, the Virgin River leads the eye straight up to the Watchman, which catches the last light after the canyon floor has gone into shade. Flat, paved, and a level walk from the visitor center.

accessNote: Zion publishes photography closures that go beyond the servicewide rule, so location matters here: "No filming or still photography is allowed within designated Wilderness or Recommended Wilderness Areas. This includes most slot canyons." Also "No filming on the West Rim Trail (including Scout Lookout and the trail to Angels Landing)" and "Riverside Walk and Narrows trails are not currently permitted." Canyon Junction Bridge is in the developed road corridor and is not on that list. Getting there: "During the shuttle season, visitors cannot drive personal vehicles on the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive" — but "No ticket, permit, or reservation needed to ride the park shuttle or enter Zion National Park" and "The park shuttle is free to ride."

name: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park
highlight: The rim drops away into the densest stand of hoodoos in the amphitheatre — thousands of orange fins and columns, with Thor's Hammer standing clear below the railing. It is a flat walk from the parking area, and at 8,000 feet the light goes warm and long well before the sun is actually down.

accessNote: No reservation system and the rim road stays open year-round, but drones are banned outright: the park states "use of remote-controlled equipment (including but not limited to helicopters, drones, and other aircraft-based equipment) within Bryce Canyon National Park is prohibited by law" (https://www.nps.gov/brca/planyourvisit/filmphotoguidelines.htm).

name: Pinnacles Overlook, Badlands National Park
highlight: A high point near the northwest end of the Badlands Loop Road where the banded spires drop away below you and the mixed-grass prairie runs flat to the horizon behind them. West-facing, so the buttes go pink and gold in the last half hour of light.

accessNote: If you are planning an actual ceremony rather than a proposal, Badlands requires a Special Use Permit and states "All permits must be submitted 45 days in advance" with a $100 non-refundable application fee (https://www.nps.gov/badl/planyourvisit/permits.htm). A three-person proposal does not trigger that.

name: Hawksbill Summit, Shenandoah National Park
highlight: The highest point in Shenandoah, a rock outcrop with a stone viewing platform and an open sweep down the Shenandoah Valley and out across the Blue Ridge. The climb from the Skyline Drive parking area is short and steep, and the summit is bare rock — no trees between you and the view.

It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

accessNote: Worth knowing if the proposal turns into a ceremony on the spot: Shenandoah needs no wedding permit when "No props, sets, decor, music, or other equipment will be used and the group size is 15 or less people," and separately bans one common prop outright — "Live flowers and plant material of any type (cut or potted) are not permitted at outdoor ceremonies in the Park" (https://www.nps.gov/shen/planyourvisit/special-use-permits.htm). Skyline Drive can close on short notice for snow, ice or fog; check park conditions before driving up.

name: Tunnel View, Yosemite National Park
highlight: You come out of the Wawona Tunnel and the whole valley is simply there — El Capitan on the left, Bridalveil Fall on the right, Half Dome closing the far end. It is a stone-walled pull-off directly off the road, so there is no hike and no excuse about the light.

fact.verbatim: All filming, still photography, and audio recording is treated the same under the new law. It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

permit.authority: National Park Service

accessNote: No reservation needed in 2026: "Yosemite National Park today announced it will no longer use a timed reservation system in 2026," concluding that "a season-wide reservation requirement is not the most effective approach for 2026" (https://www.nps.gov/yose/learn/news/yosemite-national-park-will-not-require-vehicle-reservations-in-2026.htm). Two Yosemite-specific rules to respect: "Except for casual filming by visitors, special use permits for filming are required for all filming activities in wilderness areas, no matter the group size or equipment used" — Tunnel View is roadside, not wilderness — and night photography and artificial lighting are prohibited without a permit.

name: Brandywine Falls, Cuyahoga Valley National Park
highlight: A tiered sandstone waterfall dropping into a wooded gorge, seen from a wooden boardwalk that steps down the cliff to an upper and a lower deck. Thirty minutes from downtown Cleveland, and the only national park spot on this list you can do on a weeknight after work.

fact.verbatim: All filming, still photography, and audio recording is treated the same under the new law. It does not matter whether it is commercial, non-commercial, for content creation, by a student, or conducted by media or for news gathering. In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals.

permit.authority: National Park Service

accessNote: A useful crowding tell from the park's own wedding-permit rules: Cuyahoga Valley lists Brandywine Falls as an available ceremony location but does not make it available on weekends, holidays, or during October — the falls are simply too busy then. That restriction applies to wedding permits, not to a three-person proposal, but it tells you which dates to avoid. The boardwalk decks are small and fill up (https://www.nps.gov/cuva/planyourvisit/permitsandreservations.htm).

name: Fort Jefferson, Dry Tortugas National Park
highlight: A six-sided brick fortress sitting alone on a sand key seventy miles west of Key West, ringed by a moat wall you can walk the whole way around with nothing but turquoise shallows on the other side. Read the permit note carefully — this one is not straightforward.

permit.authority: National Park Service

accessNote: Two federal pages say different things and Dry Tortugas is the stricter one. Servicewide, NPS says "In most cases, permits and fees are not required for filming, still photography, or audio recording that involves eight or fewer individuals" (https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/news/film-and-photo-permits.htm). Dry Tortugas' own permits page, last updated March 18, 2025 — after the EXPLORE Act took effect — says "Federal law requires a permit for all filming, no matter the size of the crew or the type of equipment." Call the park at 305-242-7700 and get the answer in writing before you book a photographer. Access is the other constraint: "Cars are not able to access the island. The only methods of transportation are by boat or seaplane" — the ferry and seaplane run once a day and book out weeks ahead (https://www.nps.gov/drto/planyourvisit/directions.htm).

disputed.verbatim: Federal law requires a permit for all filming, no matter the size of the crew or the type of equipment.

name: Sand Harbor Boulders, Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park
highlight: Rounded granite boulders sit right in the shallows, and the water over the white sand reads turquoise before it drops to cobalt a few yards out. Early morning the lake is glass and the Sierra rim across the water catches first light.

fact.verbatim: Photographers/videographers utilizing the park for commercial use (including but not limited to: social media influencing or promotion, print ads, movies, wedding, engagement, family, or senior photos, or any service that would normally be expected to be paid for under regular client/vendor circumstances) are required to get a photography permit.

permit.authority: Nevada Division of State Parks

crowdWindow.verbatim: From Memorial to Labor Day Sand Harbor is very popular and experiences high visitation. Those planning to visit Sand Harbor should be prepared for park closures and have an alternate destination in mind.

Applications filed later than two weeks out are automatically denied; the statewide page separately instructs applying at least 30 days ahead.

name: Spooner Lake, Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park
highlight: A small lake ringed by aspens at the top of the Spooner grade, with a flat two-mile loop trail and benches on the water. In late September the aspen stands go gold and the crowd thins to hikers heading for the Flume Trail.

name: White Domes, Valley of Fire State Park
highlight: A mile-long loop through a slot canyon that opens onto banded sandstone the color of raw salmon, streaked white and lavender. The last hour of light turns the rock the same red as the name suggests.

name: Spring Mountain Ranch State Park
highlight: A green lawn and a spring-fed creek at the foot of the Wilson Cliffs, half an hour from the Strip. The old ranch house and cottonwoods give you shade and a foreground; the sandstone escarpment does the rest at sunset.

name: Moon Caves, Cathedral Gorge State Park
highlight: Narrow bentonite clay slots you can walk into shoulder-width, opening to buff-colored spires that look poured rather than eroded. The canyon holds shade most of the day, so the light inside stays soft when everything above it is blown out.

name: Snow Canyon Scenic Overlook, Snow Canyon State Park
highlight: White Navajo sandstone lying in cross-bedded waves against black lava flow, with the canyon floor a couple hundred feet below. It was named an International Dark Sky Destination in 2025, so the same spot works after the sun is gone.

name: Dead Horse Point Overlook
highlight: A narrow neck of rock 2,000 feet above a gooseneck bend in the Colorado River, with the Canyonlands benches stepping away in red and white. The railed overlook is a short flat walk from the parking area, which matters if one of you is not expecting to be walking anywhere in particular.

name: Valley of Goblins, Goblin Valley State Park
highlight: A basin floor of thousands of mushroom-shaped hoodoos in Entrada sandstone, all roughly person-height, that you are allowed to walk freely among. It is a certified dark-sky park, so the same basin under the Milky Way is a second, different spot.

name: Buffalo Point, Antelope Island State Park
highlight: A short climb to a rock shoulder over the north end of the Great Salt Lake, with the Wasatch across the water and bison usually somewhere below you. At sunset the lake goes flat pink and the island's shadow runs out across it.

name: Bonneville Salt Flats
highlight: Thirty thousand acres of hard white salt crust with the Silver Island range on the horizon and no other reference point at all. After a shallow rain the surface mirrors the sky and the two of you are the only vertical thing in the frame.

fact.verbatim: The salt flats are used for land speed racing, archery competitions, running races, photography, videography, and scientific research projects. Public wishing to utilize the salt flats for these purposes need a special recreation or film permit from the BLM Salt Lake Field Office.

The page also notes "Motor vehicle use is limited by seasonal closure during the spring when the salt is moist or has standing water on the surface. Closure dates may vary and will be posted by sign." Call the Salt Lake Field Office before booking a photographer.

name: Hailstone Overlook, Jordanelle State Park
highlight: A bench of sagebrush above Jordanelle Reservoir with the Deer Valley ridgelines on one side and Mount Timpanogos closing the far end. Fifteen minutes from Park City's Main Street, and quiet on a weekday evening.

name: Prospect Point, Niagara Falls State Park
highlight: The railing at Prospect Point puts you at the exact lip where the American Falls turns over — close enough that the mist reaches you and the roar makes you lean in to be heard. America's oldest state park, open year round, so the winter version with frozen spray on the railings is a real option.

name: The Gorge Trail, Watkins Glen State Park
highlight: Nineteen waterfalls inside a single mile of shale gorge, with stone stairs cut into the wall and stretches of path that pass behind falling water. The light down there stays green and dim even at midday, and the noise covers everything else.

name: Middle Falls, Letchworth State Park
highlight: The Genesee River drops over three major waterfalls here, running between cliffs as high as 600 feet with forest on both rims. The overlook near the Glen Iris Inn faces Middle Falls straight on, and late-day sun works the spray.

name: Lake Minnewaska Overlook, Minnewaska State Park Preserve
highlight: A clear lake held in a bowl of pale Shawangunk cliffs, with pitch pine growing straight out of the rock. A carriage road loops the whole rim, so there are a dozen places to stop where the water sits directly below and the Catskills fill the far horizon.

name: Breakneck Ridge, Hudson Highlands State Park Preserve
highlight: A scramble straight up bare rock out of the river gorge near Cold Spring, with the Hudson bending south below you and Storm King directly across the water. The payoff ledges come early and fast.

name: Montauk Point State Park and Lighthouse Bluff

name: Pier 1 Granite Prospect, Brooklyn Bridge Park
highlight: Wide granite steps stepping down toward the East River, aimed straight at Lower Manhattan with the Brooklyn Bridge off to the right. It is one of the three spots the park will actually permit a ceremony, so the sightline has been thought about.

name: Bow Bridge, Central Park

name: Bethesda Terrace, Central Park
highlight: The lower arcade under the terrace has a ceiling of patterned Minton tiles and carries sound the way a chapel does, which is why buskers set up there. Step through the arch and the Angel of the Waters is straight ahead with the Lake behind her.
